prediction.change_reason: The new request_count check marks every prior finding that requests a contested candidate ambiguous, without checking whether the remaining candidate sets admit a unique one-to-one assignment. The prior sequential matcher would associate the single-path prior finding with app.py and then associate the remaining prior finding with helper.py.

evidence.basis: Candidate requests are counted, then any prior finding with a candidate requested by more than one prior is marked ambiguous, even when another candidate makes the overall one-to-one assignment unique. A direct _associate reproduction with the trigger above returns no associations and marks both prior IDs ambiguous.

prediction.impact: Both prior findings become unverified, both confirmed current findings are listed as new, and the aggregate recheck becomes partial despite a unique path-supported association. This creates duplicate review items and prevents a clean completed recheck.
prediction.root_cause: The fallback matcher treats any shared candidate as ambiguity instead of solving the one-to-one candidate assignment; a finding with a unique candidate is rejected even when the competing prior finding has a distinct remaining candidate.
prediction.trigger: Two prior and two current findings have identical normalized semantic fields; prior evidence paths are {app.py} and {app.py, helper.py}, while current evidence paths are {app.py} and {helper.py} respectively.

Client exceptions are displayed as request failures and return None, so pool exhaustion drops the UI operation.

prediction.root_cause: The Streamlit-cached HTTPX client is shared across sessions but is limited to 10 total connections with a 2-second pool timeout.
prediction.trigger: Ten requests occupy all shared connections for more than 2 seconds while another UI session starts a request.

prediction.root_cause: The 300-second report cache wraps _safe_get, which converts request failures into a cacheable None result.
prediction.trigger: A selected task is reported as completed or failed by the status-only request, then the first full-report request times out, returns an HTTP error, or fails while decoding JSON.
